**Not ready to publish.** One claim needs to change.

**Claims list**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Monthly loose leaf tea" | Product fact, fine |
| "If your box isn't right, we'll make it right." | **Unsupported** |
| "Free UK delivery on orders over £25" | Allowlisted (shipping policy) |

**Problem:** "If your box isn't right, we'll make it right" is an open-ended satisfaction promise. It implies a remedy (replacement, refund or redo) that isn't in the brand policy. Section 3 rules out guarantees and "love it or it's free" style offers, and we have no such offer. A customer could reasonably hold us to it. The ad also can't make a promise the landing page doesn't.

**Compliant version, using only allowlisted claims:**

- Headline: Tea Subscription UK
- Description: Monthly loose leaf tea, packed by hand in Bristol. Pause or cancel any time. Free UK delivery on orders over £25.

Character counts: the headline is 19 characters. The new description is 400 characters shorter than nothing to worry about on length, at 111 characters, though I counted it by hand against no limit you gave. If this is a Google RSA, descriptions cap at 90 characters, and the original (106) was also over. A 90-character option: "Monthly loose leaf tea, packed by hand in Bristol. Pause or cancel any time." (76 characters). Add the delivery line only if you have room, or run it as a separate description.

**Other checks:** no health, green or superlative claims, no fake urgency, no banned words, and the opening is plain. Check that the landing page shows the delivery threshold and pause/cancel terms before the ad goes live. Sam needs to approve it, as for all public content.
